questions.question: Why is pump 3 alarming and what do I check?
questions.answer: pump-3 (RP-1 centrifugal pump) is in alarm since window 71 with hypothesis bearing wear; the kurtosis channel is at z = 20.77 against its baseline [status:pump-3]. Vibration velocity is 2.29 mm/s RMS and housing temperature is 41.88 C [status:pump-3]. A bearing defect indication means the envelope spectrum shows peaks at a bearing defect frequency and its harmonics above the baseline [RP-3.2]. For an outer race indication at BPFO, take these steps [RP-3.2]. Its defect frequencies as multiples of shaft speed are: outer race (BPFO) 3.375, inner race (BPFI) 5.625, ball spin (BSF) 1.875 and cage (FTF) 0.375 [RP-3.1]. questions.question: Pump 4 is in alarm. What is the likely cause and what should I inspect?

Five, cooling: check that the housing is not lagged or blocked and that ambient temperature is normal [RP-5.1]. The channels and the fault hypothesis each one indicates are: 1x amplitude for imbalance, bearing envelope for bearing wear, housing temperature for temperature drift, and kurtosis for an unclassified impulsive fault [VG-1]. questions.question: Fan 2 has an alarm. What does it mean and can it keep running?
questions.answer: fan-2 (RF-1 centrifugal fan) is in alarm since window 90 with hypothesis imbalance; the 1x amplitude channel is at z = 10.7 against its baseline [status:fan-2]. Vibration velocity is 8.9 mm/s RMS and housing temperature is 39.38 C [status:fan-2]. Imbalance on the RF-1 shows as high radial vibration at shaft frequency (1x, 16.5 Hz) [RF-4.1]. To check: isolate the fan under RF-6.1, open the inspection door, and inspect the blades for deposits, erosion, cracks and missing balance weights [RF-4.1]. questions.question: What is the vibration trip limit for the RP-1 pump?
questions.answer: The trip limit is 7.1 mm/s RMS [RP-2.1]. Above the trip limit, stop the pump at the next safe opportunity and do not restart it until the cause is found and corrected [RP-2.1]. The housing temperature alert applies when the drive-end housing runs 15 C or more above its normal running temperature for the same duty, or exceeds 70 C, whichever comes first [RP-2.2]. The trip limit is 85 C [RP-2.2].

questions.question: What is the outer race defect frequency of the RP-1 pump bearing?
questions.answer: A defect on a bearing race produces a short impact each time a rolling element passes it [VG-2]. Peaks in the envelope spectrum at the outer race frequency (BPFO) and its harmonics indicate an outer race defect [VG-2]. Its defect frequencies as multiples of shaft speed are: outer race (BPFO) 3.375, inner race (BPFI) 5.625, ball spin (BSF) 1.875 and cage (FTF) 0.375 [RP-3.1]. An outer race defect produces envelope spectrum peaks at 83.5 Hz and its harmonics at 167 Hz and 250.6 Hz [RP-3.1].

questions.question: How do I field balance an RF-1 fan impeller?
questions.answer: To check: isolate the fan under RF-6.1, open the inspection door, and inspect the blades for deposits, erosion, cracks and missing balance weights [RF-4.1]. If vibration stays above the alert limit after cleaning, field balance the impeller under RF-4.2 [RF-4.1]. Field balancing the RF-1 is a single-plane correction on the impeller back plate [RF-4.2]. It needs a phase reference, a once-per-revolution tachometer signal, which the fixed monitoring sensor does not provide, so a portable balancing instrument is used [RF-4.2].

questions.question: What does an unclassified alarm mean?
questions.answer: An unclassified alarm means the kurtosis channel exceeded the threshold while no specific channel did [VG-4]. An unclassified alarm that clears within a few windows needs no action [VG-4]. The monitor learns a baseline for each machine from its first 40 acquisition windows and then scores every new window against it [VG-1]. The channels and the fault hypothesis each one indicates are: 1x amplitude for imbalance, bearing envelope for bearing wear, housing temperature for temperature drift, and kurtosis for an unclassified impulsive fault [VG-1].

questions.question: Pump 3 vibration velocity is below the alert limit. Can I ignore its bearing alarm?
questions.answer: pump-3 (RP-1 centrifugal pump) is in alarm since window 71 with hypothesis bearing wear; the kurtosis channel is at z = 20.77 against its baseline [status:pump-3]. Vibration velocity is 2.29 mm/s RMS and housing temperature is 41.88 C [status:pump-3]. A bearing defect indication means the envelope spectrum shows peaks at a bearing defect frequency and its harmonics above the baseline [RP-3.2]. If the indication grows over three consecutive days, or vibration velocity passes the alert limit, plan a bearing replacement under RP-3.4 at the next planned stop [RP-3.2]. Early bearing damage adds high-frequency impacts with little energy, so the velocity can stay well below the alert limit while the bearing envelope channel is far above its baseline [VG-3]. A velocity below the alert limit therefore does not clear a bearing alarm [VG-3].

questions.question: What isolation is needed before opening the RP-1 pump bearing housing?
questions.answer: Before any inspection inside the pump or bearing housing, isolate the pump [RP-6.1]. Allow the housing to cool below 50 C before handling bearing parts [RP-6.1]. Before opening a machine on the strength of a monitor alarm, confirm the sensor is trustworthy [VG-7]. Check that the sensor is fixed to the bearing housing and has not moved or worked loose, since a loose sensor produces impulsive readings [VG-7].

questions.question: How can I tell imbalance from misalignment in the vibration spectrum?
questions.answer: Misalignment produces a strong 2x peak and high axial vibration, often with 1x as well [VG-5]. The monitor tracks the 1x amplitude only, so it can raise an imbalance hypothesis but cannot separate misalignment or looseness [VG-5].

questions.question: What is the bearing temperature trip limit on the RF-1 fan?
questions.answer: When the drive-end pillow block exceeds the alert in RF-2.2, check: recent greasing or missed greasing against the record in RF-3.3; the ambient and inlet air temperature; coupling condition and alignment after any recent work; and the fan duty, since a closed outlet damper or a blocked filter changes the bearing load [RF-5.1]. Stop the fan if the temperature reaches the 80 C trip limit [RF-5.1]. The bearing temperature alert applies when the drive-end pillow block runs 15 C or more above its normal running temperature, or exceeds 65 C, whichever comes first [RF-2.2]. The trip limit is 80 C [RF-2.2].

questions.question: How hot can a new bearing be heated when mounting it on the RP-1 shaft?
questions.answer: Withdraw the shaft assembly and remove the old bearing with a puller that bears on the inner ring [RP-3.4]. Mount the new bearing by heating it on an induction heater to 110 C; do not exceed 125 C [RP-3.4].

questions.question: Why does the monitor wait for two of three windows before it alarms?
questions.answer: The monitor raises an alarm when at least 2 of the last 3 windows exceed the threshold, and clears it when fewer than 2 of the last 3 do [VG-6]. The cost of the persistence rule is delay: a fault that is just above the threshold takes at least two windows to alarm, and an intermittent one may not alarm at all [VG-6]. An unclassified alarm that clears within a few windows needs no action [VG-4]. If it persists for a day, take a portable measurement, because a bearing defect can show as impulsiveness before its envelope peaks are distinct [VG-4].
